lede: A tech-led rout knocked the S&P 500 down 3.7% on Friday, capping a weekly slide of about 8.6%, as Nvidia sank 14% on a reported SEC accounting review and the Nasdaq lost 5.3%. Gold fell for a ninth straight session to about $3,538, and Bitcoin ended the week below $60,000 for the first time since July.
snapshot_time: Fri 20 Nov close (NY 17:00 ET = 01:00 TRT Sat) · FX/gold markets closed for the weekend

focus.text: Lost 2.4% to about $3,538 on Friday after dipping to $3,503, as near-certain December Fed hike bets and stock-rout deleveraging hit; roughly 8.5% down on the week. Monday's flash PMIs are the next test.

Finished the week just under 1.10, near 19-month lows, as Fed hike pricing kept the dollar firm despite softer US yields. 1.0950 is nearby support; Monday's euro-area and US flash PMIs are the first risk.

technicals.indicators: Hourly RSI ≈ 16–18 on Friday (deeply oversold) · well below 50- and 200-day MAs · nine straight losing sessions
technicals.note: Gold has cut through the 3,600 shelf to a 14-month low, extending the run of lower highs from the early-November peak near 4,158.

technicals.indicators: RSI(14) H4 ≈ 42 · Stochastic ≈ 17 (oversold) · MACD below zero · at lower Bollinger band
technicals.note: The pair is compressing just below the 1.10 handle near 19-month lows; the former 1.10 support now acts as a ceiling.
Cable lost its 1.3138 pivot and is probing the one-year-low zone around 1.3080, keeping the lower-high, lower-low sequence intact.

technicals.indicators: ≈21% below 200-day MA (~75,100) · 50-day MA ~74,500 · Fear & Greed 11–16 (extreme fear)
technicals.note: Bitcoin broke the 60,000–62,000 floor that held since mid-November and is now testing its July lows without a daily higher low.
SOL gave up the $70 handle and sits on its monthly low, deep in oversold territory after a steady series of lower highs.

news.text: S&P 500 fell 3.7% to 6,910 and the Nasdaq 5.3%; S&P and Dow closed in correction as Nvidia slid 14% on a reported SEC accounting probe and chipmakers lost 9–14%.
Governor Cook said delaying hikes risks falling behind the curve and Philadelphia's Paulson is open to back-to-back moves; a 9 Dec hike is priced at roughly 90% or more.
Haven buying cut the US 10-year yield about 10 bp to near 4.91%; the dollar index eased to ~103.84 after Thursday's 19-month high.
Final November UMich sentiment rose to 51.5 from October's 48.0, while one-year inflation expectations cooled to 3.7%.
Brent settled 0.6% higher at $92.57 on Iran-related supply worries, while WTI ($83.98) still logged a third weekly decline.
Bitcoin dropped through $60,000 for the first time since early July as the Wall Street sell-off spread, briefly reaching about $57,700 near its 12-month low.
Spot BTC ETFs saw $582.3M of net outflows on 19 Nov, $541.1M from BlackRock's fund, a third straight day; November redemptions total about $3.5B.
Around $1.33B of positions were liquidated in 24 hours on Friday, roughly 90% of them longs; open interest fell about 5.6%.
No altcoin spot ETF attracted inflows on 20 Nov; XRP funds shed $4.97M and Solana funds $5.90M, per SoSoValue.
Ether lost about 7% to near $1,620, its lowest since July, underperforming Bitcoin; the Fear & Greed index sits in extreme fear (11–16).
CoinShares disclosed it sold its entire corporate Ether holding and half of its Solana treasury earlier in the week.
